sources.title: Initial motility and vitality predict the semen quality after long-term cryostorage, even in patients with restricted ejaculate parameters
sources.authors: Bier S, Hanke D, Zitzmann M, Kliesch S, Nordhoff V
sources.claim: 293 men with samples stored 2.5 to more than 14 years: storage duration did not change post-thaw motility, vitality or morphology; initial motility and concentration predicted post-thaw quality. Freezing itself lowered progressive motility from 44.3% to 25.0%.
sources.quote: no changes in motility (p = 0.44), vitality (p = 0.08), or morphology (p = 0.44) across the cohorts ... progressive motility fell from 44.3% at baseline to 25.0% after the first post-thaw test

sources.title: The impact of cryopreserved sperm on intrauterine insemination outcomes: is frozen as good as fresh?
sources.claim: 5,335 IUI cycles (1,871 frozen, 3,464 fresh): unadjusted clinical pregnancy 9.4% frozen vs 13.0% fresh; after adjustment not significant overall (OR 0.77); time to pregnancy longer with frozen (3.84 vs 2.58 cycles); live birth and cumulative pregnancy similar.
sources.quote: clinical outcomes did not differ significantly between frozen and fresh sperm IUI cycles

sources.title: Sperm banking in testicular cancer survivors: Low utilization, high costs, and patient-reported barriers from a Canadian cohort
sources.authors: Lu S, Ko Y, Fathy M, Patel P
sources.claim: Canadian cohort (24 survey respondents): 13% used their banked sperm; mean cost about $2,000 over three years; 58% found the cost burdensome; 50% felt time pressure deciding.
sources.quote: Only three men (13%) used their cryopreserved sperm ... The mean cost was approximately $2000 over three years, and 58% found this burdensome.

sources.title: Cancer and its impact on sperm, cryopreservation, and fertility (ASRM patient fact sheet, revised 2023)
sources.claim: Collection is simple and noninvasive; sperm is mixed with cryoprotectants and frozen; sperm can be stored indefinitely, and sperm frozen more than 20 years has produced pregnancies; more than one sample may be requested; very few sperm are needed with IVF.
sources.quote: Sperm can be stored indefinitely ... very few sperm are necessary to fertilize an egg in a dish

sources.title: Fertility preservation in patients with medical indications: a committee opinion (2026)
sources.claim: Ejaculated semen cryopreservation is an established technology for postpubertal males; ideally multiple samples; affordability is a key barrier; all health insurance should cover established fertility preservation.
sources.quote: For postpubertal males, ejaculated semen cryopreservation is an established technology ... Ideally, multiple samples should be obtained ... Affordability is a key barrier ... All health insurance should cover established fertility preservation services.

sources.title: FAQ: Health Insurance Coverage for Infertility, Fertility Preservation, and Surrogacy
sources.journal: New York State Department of Financial Services
sources.claim: NY-regulated individual, small group and large group policies must cover fertility preservation when a medical treatment (surgery, radiation, chemotherapy or other, including hormone therapy) may cause infertility; covered services include collecting, freezing, preserving and storing sperm; no specific storage time limit; self-funded employer plans are excluded.
sources.quote: the collecting, freezing, preserving, and storing of ova or sperm ... The fertility preservation law does not include a specific limit on the duration of storage for ova or sperm.
